name: cancho
tagline: Tools built for agents, not adapted from humans: a native systems language, and the ecosystem built with it, where trust comes from verification, not comprehension.

stages.alpha: Runs, may change, not for production.
stages.early: Built and tested, with named gaps.
stages.built: Code exists and is documented; its README does not name a stage.
stages.design: A design or plan; little or nothing is built.

projects.name: cancho
projects.summary: The language and its Rust compiler. A second compiler, written in cancho, is being checked against it.

projects.name: cancho-ui
projects.summary: A UI language whose compiler knows what each component is allowed to do. Builds JavaScript and DOM.
projects.authority: a component declares `requires Clock;`; a missing or unused declaration is refused (capability-missing, capability-unused)

projects.name: cancho-hooks
projects.summary: Webhook delivery: on disk before the 202, signed, retried, dead-lettered and replayable.

projects.name: cancho-cache
projects.summary: Redis-compatible cache over RESP2 and RESP3: strings and hashes, expiry and LRU eviction, in a fixed arena.
projects.authority: reads one file (/dev/urandom, for the hash seed); no FFI; checked in CI
projects.note: Answers 69 of Redis 7.0's 240 commands; no persistence, replication or TLS; not a Redis replacement.

projects.name: cancho-gateway
projects.summary: An HTTP/1.1 reverse proxy you can audit: strict, bounded request parsing, no FFI, a checkable authority report.
projects.note: A working slice, not a finished one. The report proves it touches no files and no foreign code; the upstream set is compiled in and enforced by exact match, but the compiler does not vouch for it.

projects.name: cancho-mqtt
projects.summary: An MQTT broker you can reason about: 3.1.1 over plain TCP, QoS 0 to 2, retained messages, wills and persistent sessions, on one thread with bounded memory.
projects.authority: cannot touch a file, dial out or call foreign code (proved by the compiler)
projects.note: Alpha, for a trusted network: plain TCP, in memory, no TLS, no long soak run.

projects.name: cancho-dns
projects.summary: A forwarding and caching DNS resolver: a bounded packet parser, an answer cache in a fixed arena, no FFI.
projects.note: Its README still says design stage. Built so far: the codec, a UDP and TCP server, an answer cache, a forwarder and an access list with response-rate limiting. No benchmark yet.

projects.name: cancho-oci
projects.summary: Container images without a daemon: oci-build assembles a reproducible FROM-scratch image from static executables.
projects.authority: no network in its authority report

projects.name: cancho-pg
projects.summary: PostgreSQL client: v3 protocol, SCRAM-SHA-256, extended queries, TLS, non-blocking pool.
projects.authority: network and heap only; no C or foreign calls

projects.name: cancho-schema
projects.summary: Schemas as data: validation, problem+json errors and JSON Schema 2020-12 from one value.

projects.name: cancho-web
projects.summary: Typed routes, validated bodies, problem+json errors and an OpenAPI document from one declaration.
projects.note: The declaration half of the framework is built.

projects.name: cancho-log
projects.summary: A durable, segmented, append-only log with crash-safe recovery that cuts off a torn tail.
projects.note: Append path only; not a Kafka replacement.

projects.name: cancho-stats
projects.summary: Statistics whose last digit you can check: a command line for describing data and drawing inferences, with exact sums and error bounds written before the code.
projects.note: Its page replays two real runs of stats describe.

projects.name: cancho-ml
projects.summary: Classical machine learning on tabular data as a command line an agent can read: seven models, one JSON line out, or a named refusal with a repair.

projects.name: cancho-tools
projects.summary: Ten small tools for agents (seek, list, peek, jsonq, tally, hash, write, replace, move, archive) and one opt-in, run. JSON out, tagged refusals that often carry a repair.
projects.note: Not claimed: that agents do better with them than with the usual tools. That evaluation has not been run.

projects.name: cancho-table
projects.summary: Select, filter, group and aggregate CSV/TSV for agents; bounded, exact, byte-stable.

projects.name: cancho-robot
projects.summary: A robot arm controller: the Feetech servo bus, SO-101 kinematics and a safety core every motion goes through.

projects.name: cancho-gpu
projects.summary: A compiler for typed tile kernels (.chx) to CUDA C and Metal, written in cancho; it also runs language models on a Metal GPU.
projects.note: Per its README: Qwen2.5-0.5B and a 27B model agree with reference implementations.

projects.name: cancho-code
projects.summary: An AI coding assistant that proves its work: the cancho compiler checks every piece the model writes, and a task is done only when the compiler and the task's own examples say so.
projects.note: Its README reports 38 of 39 units verified on 13 small libraries built from hand-written plans (Claude Haiku 5.5, hidden tests); conditions and caveats are in its eval/results.

projects.name: cancho-forge
projects.summary: An agent-run software company you can audit: state, budgets, approvals and evidence are kept by the runtime, and a worker cannot accept its own work.
projects.authority: the dispatcher holds an Exec narrowed to the worker's own programs; no filesystem, no network (Milestone 0 spike)
projects.note: Milestone 1's core only: a task state machine, an append-only journal with crash recovery, snapshots, and a read-only status and history.

projects.name: cancho-hdl
projects.summary: One .chw file declares the software/hardware boundary (registers, fields, interrupts, DMA); it is checked, and a C header, device tree, SystemVerilog RTL and CMSIS-SVD are generated from it.
projects.note: Being ported from Python to cancho: the parser, validator and checker are ported; the generators, diff and report are still Python.

projects.name: cancho-client-gen
projects.summary: Reads the OpenAPI 3.1 document that cancho-web generates and writes strictly typed clients; the contract, both ways.
projects.authority: the clients it writes make no foreign call

projects.name: cancho-fetch
projects.summary: An agent-safe fetch: HTTP and HTTPS to a fixed, built-in list of hosts, with the list in the binary's authority row instead of a flag.
projects.note: Design only; the host matching it needs is in review in cancho (#561).

projects.name: cancho-mqtt-client
projects.summary: An MQTT 3.1.1 client library: connect, publish, subscribe, will, QoS 0 and 1, and a reconnect with bounded backoff. The other half of cancho-mqtt.

figures.what: conformance tests pass when every build goes through the compiler written in cancho; the other 7 are known differences from the Rust compiler, each listed
programs that must be refused are refused by the cancho compiler with the same rule as the Rust one; it does not yet check everything
named rules, stable tags a program can match on

verifies.stamp: Counted at cancho 1d4c44e, 2026-10-20. Each line links its evidence; a claim found false is corrected here, in place.
verifies.disclaimer: A passing check shows that the checks listed here passed. It does not show a program is correct or secure in every respect, and tests exercise the behaviour they cover, not all behaviour. None of this is a certification, and no independent audit is claimed.

compiler.claim: A value is consumed exactly once. A resource left unconsumed is refused as `linear-value-unconsumed` (19 refusal fixtures).
Effect rows are exact. Performing an effect the signature does not declare is refused as `effect-not-declared` (12 fixtures); declaring one that is not performed is refused too.
Authority is derived, not declared: `cancho authority` lists what a program can reach, and says “unbounded” when foreign code is reachable.
Every refusal carries a stable rule tag, and `--output json` gives it as data.
Each declaration has a content hash (`cancho ids`); dependencies pin to hashes.

tests.claim: 359 refusal fixtures, each naming the rule it must be refused with, and 123 accepting programs.
The conformance suite builds and runs real programs; the gate (format, clippy, tests) runs on linux-x86_64 and darwin-aarch64.
Every checked code block in AGENTS.md is a fixture; changing a rule name to a wrong one turns the suite red (checked by doing it).

A mutation fuzzer feeds token-level edits of every program through parsing, checking and code generation, requiring no panic, a stable print-and-parse, and that what the checker accepts the backend compiles.
Tests are checked by breaking what they cover and watching them fail.
With every build going through the compiler written in cancho, 697 of 704 conformance tests pass (measured 2026-10-15, macOS aarch64).

open.claim: The compiler written in cancho refuses 256 of the 333 programs that must be refused, with the same rule as the Rust one. It is not the default.
Hash stability is not a contract yet: the canonical-AST document is “proposed”, and 39% of this repository’s own historical revisions do not type-check under today’s build.

A cancho program has one network bound shared by listening and connecting, so a proxy’s authority report cannot say which upstreams it reaches; cancho-gateway enforces its compiled-in list by exact match and tests it, but the compiler does not vouch for it.
The TLS stack is not independently reviewed (stated in cancho-fetch’s README).
Not evaluated: whether agents do better with cancho-tools than with the usual tools. That needs an agent-in-the-loop evaluation that has not been run.
Pre-1.0, supported on linux-x86_64 and darwin-aarch64 only, and its own README says it is not a usable language yet.

paths.blurb: Hardware, GPUs and robotics. Experimental: read each status before you rely on it.
